correctness.rationale: The order ideal of P=[2]×[3]×[4] is uniquely a legal monotone 2×3 array of heights in {0,...,4}; independently wrote a complete recursion checking all height arrays and obtained exactly 490 distinct 24-bit masks. On all 2^24=16,777,216 characters I independently computed exact 24-stage Walsh coefficients with 442 distinct signed values, 1,234,934 zeros, 15,542,282 nonzero, nonzero extremes 2 and 490, and Parseval total squares 490*2^24=8,220,835,840. I applied a second all-coordinate integer transform to the Boolean support mask, independently obtaining numerator sum |H(x)| =11,078,918,348 and H(0)=15,542,282, support Parseval 15,542,282*2^24=260,756,222,246,912. Thus ratio 11,078,918,348/16,777,216 reduces to 2,769,729,587/4,194,304. For arbitrary linear projections, translation averaging onto the invariant Fourier range gives the unique Fourier-support projector, proving unrestricted minimality analytically. These are complete finite-24bit calculations; no claim about all boxes.

value.rationale: Boxed plane partitions and their order ideals/lozenge tilings are canonical objects; the 2×3×4 box is the smallest nontrivial three-dimensional box with mutually distinct side lengths. Its 490 unweighted count is classical, but the entire 24-coordinate binary signed frequency distribution, sharp zero support and projector amplification are independently useful exact invariant data for a natural constrained-height ensemble. Complete finite classification rather than an arbitrary selected slice, with no higher-box extrapolation.
